12.0.s.en: (1) The priests and Levites who returned from the captivity

12.0.0.en: Nehemiah takes care to set down these lists of the priests, followed by the Levites, in honor of them for their faithfulness, and on the other hand so that this may always be an incentive to the priests and Levites who serve in his days in the Temple to do their service with faithfulness and spiritual zeal. There is also the greatness of these leaders, for they left the powerful land of the captivity and came to Jerusalem in ruins, for the sake of God and His worship.

12.0.1.en: It mentions to us the chief priests who returned with Zerubbabel in 536 BC to Jerusalem; they were only four chiefs (Ezra 2:36-39), but Zerubbabel divided them into 22 courses, whereas the prophet David had divided the priests into 24 courses (1 Chr 24:8). Jeshua, mentioned in (v. 1), is the supreme head of all the priests.

12.0.2.en: Abijah, mentioned in (v. 4), is the ancestor of John the Baptist (Lk 1:5).

12.1.0.en: It mentions to us the Levites responsible for works in the Temple, which are:

12.1.1.en: 1- Thanksgiving, or praise, that is, chanting the Psalms.

12.1.2.en: 2- Guarding the gates of the Temple.

12.2.0.en: It gives us a list of the names of the high priests throughout the period of Persian rule, beginning with Jeshua, who returned from the captivity with Zerubbabel, down to Jehoiada, who was in the days of Nehemiah, and whose grandson was also called Jaddua. He is the one who received Alexander the Great in the year 322 BC, wearing his priestly garments, and informed him of the prophecy of Daniel concerning the rise of the Greek empire. Alexander had seen the appearance of this priest in a dream the night before, so there came to be goodwill between Alexander and the Jews. He considered that the God of Israel blessed his steps, and so he drew back from conquering Jerusalem. All this is reported from Josephus the historian. It is noted that this list does not contain all the high priests, but some were omitted.

12.3.0.en: Here it mentions a list of the chief priests who were in the days of Nehemiah, each of whom represented a course of the priests, and it mentions his great-grandfather, who was in the days of Zerubbabel, such as “Of Seraiah, Meraiah”: Seraiah was the chief priest in the days of Zerubbabel (v. 1) and Meraiah his grandson was the chief priest in the days of Nehemiah (v. 12...), and so on.

12.3.1.en: Here Nehemiah takes care to mention the chief priests, to whom history began to be ascribed after the captivity, when they had no king; for anciently, before the captivity, history was ascribed to the kings of Judah and Israel.

12.4.0.en: Here it mentions with care the Levites as heads of fathers' houses in the days of Eliashib the high priest in the time of Nehemiah's governorship of Jerusalem. This is because the role of the priests had grown weak in this period and the role of the Levites in the service had grown strong, so they were counted as heads of fathers' houses. Their role was shown in the explanation of the Law in (ch. 8:7) and the leading of prayer (ch. 9:4, 5), for God does not leave Himself without a witness.

12.4.1.en: Some courses of the Levites were responsible for praise, and each course was divided so that it had its turn, that is, a part in which it carried out the praise before the Temple of God. Perhaps the course was divided into two sections, one chanting a portion of the Psalm and the other responding to it according to the command of David (1 Chr 23:30). There were also other courses of the Levites for guarding.

12.4.2.en: How great it is that you carry out your service, for it is precious in the eyes of God because it is offered out of love for Him. Do not be distracted from it by the vain affairs of life, as the priests were distracted in the days of Nehemiah. God did not forsake His people when the Levites rose with zeal to serve His house, and He will send someone to care for them, but you will lose the blessing.

12.5.s.en: (2) The dedication of the wall of Jerusalem

12.5.0.en: Dedication: consecrating or setting apart a place or a thing to God by special prayers.

12.5.1.en: Nehemiah took care to gather the Levites from all the places in which they dwelt around Jerusalem, to come and take part in the dedication of the wall. They had returned to their places after keeping the Feast of Tabernacles, and it was necessary to summon them to share with the priests and the people in this dedication, for the dedication is not proper without the servants appointed for it.

12.5.2.en: The dedication of the wall was important for the following reasons:

12.5.3.en: 1- To thank God, who helped them and completed the building for them.

12.5.4.en: 2- To acknowledge that God is the protector of Jerusalem by His blessing of the wall.

12.5.5.en: 3- The city of Jerusalem and its wall are dedicated to God, and it is not proper that any work against God be done in it, such as the worship of idols.

12.5.6.en: The dedication is a joyful act, and so it was accompanied by musical instruments with words of praise, and all were in joy because of the great work of God with them.

12.6.0.en: Before entering into the rite of dedication, all who took part in it had to be purified, and those who carried out the purification were the priests and Levites, who purified the people, the wall and the gates. Therefore the priest and the servant must be purified by cleansing his heart, and by repentance, before undertaking any service.

12.6.1.en: The purification of a person is by sprinkling the water of purification, as the Law of Moses commanded (Num 8:7; 19:9), and the purification of the wall and the gates is by sprinkling the water of purification upon it.

12.6.2.en: This purification signifies, in the New Testament, the examining of the soul, repentance and confession, so that a person may be able to approach to partake of the Holy Mysteries.

12.7.0.en: “Went”: it walked at a slow pace.

12.7.1.en: Nehemiah divided the priests, the Levites and the rulers into two companies. One company, led by Ezra the priest, went from the south of Jerusalem toward the northeast until it reached the Temple, which lies in the north of Jerusalem; it walked to the right on the wall, that is, counterclockwise. The second company moved from the south of Jerusalem and walked on top of the wall toward the west and then the north until it reached the Temple; that is, it walked to the left on the wall, clockwise. Thus the two companies moved from one place and met at the end at the Temple, because the wall was great in length and therefore needed two companies, the first under the hand of Ezra and the second under the leadership of Nehemiah himself. This means that the wall was broad enough to allow rows of people to walk on it side by side.

12.7.2.en: We see Nehemiah's humility: he walks behind his company, but he put Ezra at the head of the second company in honor of him.

12.7.3.en: And the people walked on the ground inside the walls of Jerusalem, praying and chanting the Psalms of David alongside the company with which they walked.

12.7.4.en: In these verses we see that Nehemiah placed corresponding groups in each of the two companies, as the following table shows:

12.7.5.en: A table showing the two companies that carried out the dedication of the wall. The first company. The second company

12.7.6.en: 1- Led by Ezra. 1- Nehemiah behind it

12.7.7.en: 2- The company of the singers of praise. 2- The company of the singers of praise

12.7.8.en: 3- Half of the princes of Judah. 3- Half of the rulers

12.7.9.en: 4- The sons of the priests with trumpets. 4- The priests with trumpets

12.7.10.en: 5- Seven priests from Azariah to Jeremiah. 5- Seven priests from Eliakim to Hananiah

12.7.11.en: 6- Bearers of the instruments of song (the musicians). 6- The singers

12.7.12.en: 7- Zechariah and eight others. 7- Jezrahiah and eight others. Thus the dedication of the wall was completed by passing over all of it and sprinkling all of it with water, it and its gates, and prayers went up over it. The conclusion was the meeting of all who took part in the dedication, with the people behind them, in the Temple, and there they prayed and thanked God and offered sacrifices of thanksgiving, as we shall see in the following verses.

12.8.0.en: The people offered many sacrifices to God on the day of the dedication of the wall, expressing their coming to God, their sacrifice for Him and their thanksgiving to Him, because He:

12.8.1.en: 1- Helped them and completed the wall for them, to protect their city.

12.8.2.en: 2- Brought to nothing the plots of the wicked who tried to hinder the building of the wall.

12.8.4.en: 4- Gave them unity in the meeting of the civil leaders, that is, Nehemiah and all his assistants, with the spiritual leaders, who are the priests and Levites. And all were of one spirit with the people.

12.8.5.en: All that preceded expressed their feelings and filled them with joy. And when God saw their concern, which included all, men, women and children, He gave them a special grace of divine joy, which surpassed all their imagining, so that their joy was in truth a great joy.

12.8.6.en: And their strong joy appeared in a shout in a loud voice from all the people, so that it was heard from afar from Jerusalem, the holy city.

12.8.7.en: Be faithful in your responsibilities for the sake of God, and your heart will rejoice in His grace; for when you offer your feelings toward Him you receive an abundance of His love, and He gives you what He gives to no one else, namely peace and happiness, which are the pledge of the Kingdom of Heaven.

12.9.s.en: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

12.9.0.en: The chambers: the rooms attached to the Temple.

12.9.1.en: The offerings (heave offerings): everything that a person lifts up from his produce or his earnings to God, that is, the contributions, the tithes and what exceeds them, for he felt that what he offered was lifted up to God who dwells in heaven.

12.9.3.en: The people expressed their joy in God who dwelt in their midst and who completed the wall for them, so they offered all that the Law prescribed of tithes and firstfruits, and also all that exceeded it of offerings of love for God. They appointed priests and Levites in charge of the storehouses in which were gathered the various offerings of the people, which they collected from the cities of the children of Israel. Perhaps they set aside special rooms for each city; that is, they established a careful system for collecting the gifts that were used in the Temple and from which portions were given to the Levites.

12.9.4.en: What is meant by “that day” is at that time, and not a specific day, for in those days the people's faithfulness in offering their gifts to the Temple appeared.

12.9.5.en: May you express your joy not by mere emotion, but by making decisions and offering the love of God in your relationship with Him and in your service in His Church, and so your joy will be firm and you will gladden the heart of God.

12.10.0.en: The priests and Levites also expressed their joy by the following:

12.10.1.en: 1- Appointing overseers over the storehouses, as the previous verse mentioned.

12.10.2.en: 2- Keeping watch at the gates of the Temple to prevent the entrance of foreigners from the Gentiles, or of the unclean; this is the ward of purification, that is, making sure of the purity and readiness of everyone who enters the Temple.

12.10.3.en: 3- The singers carrying out their role in chanting the Psalms before the Temple, by organizing companies that took turns in their work, to offer constant prayers before God, and so that those entering the Temple might enjoy sharing in these prayers. This is what David and Solomon commanded, and Nehemiah and Ezra now restored it.

12.11.0.en: To organize the companies of singers, David anciently appointed chiefs of the singers, such as Asaph, and now in the days of Nehemiah and Ezra they too appointed chiefs of the singers, to organize the service of praise and glorification, that is, thanksgiving in the Temple.

12.12.0.en: We see the clear concern for the service of the Temple after the return from the captivity, that is, in the days of Zerubbabel and then in the days of Nehemiah, the governors who ruled over Jerusalem and Judea. They took care to provide for the material needs of the singers and gatekeepers; perhaps they assigned larger gifts to these two classes than to the rest of the Levites, and singing and guarding may have been a work in addition to sharing in the rest of the works of the Levites, which confirms that these two classes deserved larger gifts.

12.12.1.en: We see a clear concern on the part of the Levites, to whom the people give tithes and various gifts, for they in turn offer their tithes and gifts to the priests. Thus all enjoy, not only the provision of the needs of others, but, more important than this, the receiving of God's blessing in their lives.

12.12.2.en: The word “sanctify” expresses God's blessing upon all that a person possesses. He who gives tithes and gifts to God, God sanctifies all the rest that he has, so that it suffices him and overflows. The gift is a blessing to the one who gives, as it is to the one who receives, and all blessing is from the hand of God.

12.12.3.en: How beautiful it is that the Levites take care of the needs of their spiritual fathers, who are the priests, as the people took care of the needs of their spiritual guides, who are the Levites. For if all the spiritual leaders care for the spiritual needs of the people, then all the more should the people care to provide for their material needs, so that they lack nothing and are not occupied with anything away from their service, which is the most important work, as the Apostle Paul affirmed (1 Cor 9:11). Renewed purification. Nehemiah spent twelve years in Jerusalem (ch. 5:14), in which he completed the building of the wall and the spiritual care of the people, and perhaps he returned to the king once or several times in this period, but nothing is mentioned about that in the Holy Bible.

12.12.4.en: After twelve years Nehemiah returned to the king and spent a period with him whose length is not known; it may have been months or years. After it he returned to Jerusalem, because his heart was attached to it, and was surprised by the spread of evil among the people. Since Nehemiah was concerned not only with the outward fortification of Jerusalem but rather with the care of the people, his heart was deeply moved when he found them fallen into many sins, the most important of which were:

12.12.5.en: 1- Mingling with the Ammonites and Moabites.

12.12.6.en: 2- Defiling the Temple by bringing the Gentiles into it.

12.12.7.en: 3- Neglecting to collect the tithes, and so the Levites did not find their food and left the service of the Temple, and worship stopped in the Temple.

12.12.9.en: 5- Marrying idolatrous women and so becoming attached to their gods.

12.12.10.en: Despite all these corruptions Nehemiah did not despair but trusted in God and began to purify the people again and bring them back to God. What, then, were the second reforms that Nehemiah carried out?

12.12.11.en: (1) The expulsion of the Ammonites and Moabites (vv. 1-9)

12.12.12.en: 1- On that day they read in the book of Moses in the audience of the people; and therein was found written, that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever; 2- Because they met not the children of Israel with bread and with water, but hired Balaam against them, that he should curse them: howbeit our God turned the curse into a blessing. 3- Now it came to pass, when they had heard the law, that they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude. 4- And before this, Eliashib the priest, having the oversight of the chamber of the house of our God, was allied unto Tobiah: 5- And he had prepared for him a great chamber, where aforetime they laid the meat offerings, the frankincense, and the vessels, and the tithes of the corn, the new wine, and the oil, which was commanded to be given to the Levites, and the singers, and the porters; and the offerings of the priests. 6- But in all this time was not I at Jerusalem: for in the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon came I unto the king, and after certain days obtained I leave of the king:

12.12.13.en: 7- And I came to Jerusalem, and understood of the evil that Eliashib did for Tobiah, in preparing him a chamber in the courts of the house of God. 8- And it grieved me sore: therefore I cast forth all the household stuff of Tobiah out of the chamber. 9- Then I commanded, and they cleansed the chambers: and thither brought I again the vessels of the house of God, with the meat offering and the frankincense.
